title: What was wrong and what was fixed
scope: latents working-tree audit repairs; starting HEAD24773e6/version0.97.1

entries.title: Excluded rows changed membership estimates
entries.problem: An extreme predictor in a zero-weight row could affect initialization and conditioning, changing a fit even though the row contributed no likelihood.
entries.fix: Use contributing rows for centers, rank and separation checks and membership initialization.
entries.verification: Changing the excluded predictor from 0 to 10¹² now leaves the likelihood, posteriors and robust standard errors identical. The retained likelihood is −586.844083; the faulty fit had fallen to about −730.5432.

entries.title: Large count values lost likelihood information
entries.problem: Large common log-density offsets and nearly equal count means could erase class differences. The occasion-specific LTA prior path could lose information too.
entries.fix: Preserve relative log densities and calculate close mean ratios stably; center measurement contributions before adding the pooled prior in both LTA engines.
entries.verification: One posterior changed from the incorrect (0.5, 0.5) to (0.7665746545, 0.2334253455), matching the independent calculation. Near-equal-mean and LTA prior regressions pass.

entries.title: Distinct ordinal categories collapsed
entries.problem: Formatting numeric codes as text merged values such as 1,000,000,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000,000,001.
entries.fix: Retain native numeric category values, use unambiguous labels and use the native map in prediction and data comparison.
entries.verification: The reproduced model retains three distinct categories and matches the independently calculated likelihood exactly.

entries.title: Large origins were mistaken for constant data
entries.problem: A large common origin could make genuinely varying observations fail spread checks.
entries.fix: Remove the constancy cutoff tied to the raw origin and retain the centered standard-deviation calculation.
entries.verification: The reproduced case now returns SD 0.9340709706, equal to the independent calculation, instead of latents_bad_data.

entries.title: Weight checks depended on measurement units
entries.problem: Nonconstant weights scaled down to tiny numbers could pass checks that rejected the same relative weights at ordinary scale.
entries.fix: Compare weight variation using a relative constancy check, retaining the existing safe normalization.
entries.verification: The same invalid weight pattern is rejected at scales from approximately 10⁻³⁰⁰ to 10³⁰⁰.

entries.title: Extreme responses produced incorrect posteriors
entries.problem: Underflow in regression and growth calculations could produce probabilities that did not sum to one or lost the intended prior proportions.
entries.fix: Use stable shared normalization of log weights and preserve relative contributions.
entries.verification: The direct normalization example now returns the expected (0.8, 0.2), replacing the faulty (1, 0.1353) values. Public crossing-mean tests retain each fitted model’s prior proportions.

entries.title: Class matching ignored covariance and dispersion
entries.problem: Classes with similar means but different spreads could be matched by prevalence, mixing narrow and wide classes during pooling. Negative-binomial dispersion was absent from the candidate signature.
entries.fix: Include Gaussian spread/correlation and negative-binomial variance features in a shared reference scale. Keep count features finite at zero variance.
entries.verification: One pooling example changed from variances (12.38, 13.52) to (0.9403591, 24.9588584), preserving the narrow/wide classes. NB public-fit, zero-boundary and unchanged-Poisson checks pass.

entries.title: Category names collided in inference tables
entries.problem: Reserved characters in variable/category names could create identical term keys, attaching the wrong standard errors or confidence intervals to results and plots.
entries.fix: Encode reserved components consistently and match intervals using full parameter and class identity.
entries.verification: A reproduced pair of standard errors now correctly differs: 0.04 versus 0.04898979487. Collision and plotting regression checks pass.

entries.title: Additive inference was sensitive to coordinates
entries.problem: Rescaling outcomes or moving their origin could falsely make information appear singular or distort the transformation of uncertainty.
entries.fix: Construct and solve the information problem in conditioned coordinates, then transform estimates and covariance back consistently.
entries.verification: A 10⁶ unit multiplier now gives the corresponding scaling of mean and variance standard errors instead of a false singular-information refusal.

entries.title: Supplied data were not checked consistently
entries.problem: Tolerant comparisons could accept changed outcomes at a large origin; some valid representations were rejected. Trajectory checks could omit fitted columns or weights.
entries.fix: Keep strict objective-data checks, verify valid forward transformations, compare normalized weights, and validate every fitted trajectory column. Assignment-only matching recognizes actual base-R CSV serialization and rejects collisions.
entries.verification: Original data, valid chart representations and uniform weight multipliers are accepted; changed outcomes and collapsed categories are rejected. Extra unrelated distal columns remain allowed.

entries.title: Univariate covariance starts had the wrong shape
entries.problem: A full-covariance start for two profiles and one indicator could be reconstructed as one profile and two indicators.
entries.fix: Preserve profile-by-indicator dimensions when rebuilding one-dimensional covariance tables.
entries.verification: The reproduced result is now a 2 × 1 table, retaining variances 0.9782054 and 0.6983753.

entries.title: Sample-size accessors disagreed with the fitting policy
entries.problem: Some accessors and model families reported sample counts inconsistent with the fitted empty-unit policy and information-criterion convention.
entries.fix: Honor the fitted drop_empty policy: TRUE uses informative units, while FALSE intentionally counts retained units, across the repaired profile, covariate and LTA accessors.
entries.verification: Tests verify both policies, including the intended 60-versus-80 count in the reproduced case, and match the accessor count to the fitted convention.

entries.title: Missing occasions became apparent class evidence
entries.problem: An entirely unobserved occasion could contribute its prior modal class to R3STEP as if a class assignment had been observed.
entries.fix: Use a missing modal assignment and neutral emission, excluding the occasion from classification-error and pooled-prior calculations.
entries.verification: A 66-empty-row example agrees with the version with those occasions removed: likelihood gap about 3.2 × 10⁻¹².

entries.title: Large covariate offsets broke LTA R3STEP
entries.problem: A predictor shifted by 10⁸ could be called constant, and an unnecessary conversion between bases could fail as singular.
entries.fix: Check actual positive spread and use a valid centered-coordinate initialization directly.
entries.verification: Large-offset and ordinary-coordinate regression checks pass without false constancy or singularity errors.

entries.title: Likelihood-ratio comparisons could mix different objectives
entries.problem: Comparisons did not consistently enforce actual data identity, weight compatibility and matching variance/probability bounds.
entries.fix: Check the data and objective-defining controls before declaring models nested or comparable.
entries.verification: Regression tests reject mismatched data and incompatible bounds while accepting valid nested comparisons.

entries.title: Empty persons changed robust R3STEP uncertainty
entries.problem: Retained empty persons could enter basis, rank and finite-sample calculations despite contributing no measurement information.
entries.fix: Use measurement-contributing persons for the repaired objective, score, rank and CR1 calculations.
entries.verification: After adding 40 empty persons, all four checked standard-error ratios are exactly one.

entries.title: Regression fitting depended on units and origin
entries.problem: Large predictor units could change the Gaussian MLE through the numerical solver; large origins could destabilize information and predictions.
entries.fix: Use centered/scaled design charts, stable weighted solves and consistent maps to natural coefficients and predictions.
entries.verification: The Gaussian example matches glm: likelihood −125.9003875122574 and slope 2.0367617905 × 10⁻¹⁰. Additional origin tests reach 10¹²; finite-double cancellation at that scale remains documented.

entries.title: Slope size was confused with separation
entries.problem: Rescaling a predictor could trigger a separation warning even when fitted logits represented an ordinary finite model. Ordinal checks had a related raw-slope sensitivity.
entries.fix: Base the diagnostic on fitted logits and the conditioned design rather than raw coefficient units.
entries.verification: The reproduced binomial model matches glm and is correctly classified as nonseparated; ordinal rescaling tests also pass.

entries.title: Brownian predictions accepted invalid times
entries.problem: Negative process times could reach prediction covariance calculations outside the Brownian model domain.
entries.fix: Validate process times before constructing predictions.
entries.verification: Negative times now raise an informative refusal; valid prediction cases pass.

entries.title: Growth caching merged different covariance designs
entries.problem: Rounded Gram-matrix cache keys could make distinct designs reuse one covariance calculation.
entries.fix: Use exact design/Gram identity for cache reuse.
entries.verification: A regression test with distinct matrices that previously shared a rounded key now keeps them separate.

entries.title: Growth predictions rebuilt a different design
entries.problem: Transformed random effects such as poly(time, 2), or ordered-factor contrasts, could be recomputed with a different basis on new data.
entries.fix: Retain fitted terms/prediction variables, factor levels and contrasts and reuse the training blueprint.
entries.verification: The polynomial-basis check has zero design error. Ordered-factor prediction and spread tests pass.

entries.title: Plot grids violated predictor structure
entries.problem: A class-curve grid could vary a membership or group-constant predictor in a way inconsistent with the fitted design.
entries.fix: Build grids that respect the predictor level and use valid fitted design information.
entries.verification: Regression tests and rendered plot previews cover class curves with membership predictors.

entries.title: Distinct numeric IDs were merged for grouping or display
entries.problem: Values such as 0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2 have different native values but the same short printed label. Text-based grouping could merge their clusters, sequences or facets.
entries.fix: Use native-value group indices and preserve distinct facets; refuse ambiguous identity reconstructions where necessary.
entries.verification: ICC, sequence and facet regressions distinguish the units. An independent ICC example is 149/152.

entries.title: Unavailable replication evidence looked reassuring
entries.problem: A candidate without a known repeated-maximum count could receive a reassuring visual status.
entries.fix: Show “replication unavailable” explicitly and explain that repeated maxima do not prove a global optimum.
entries.verification: Reporting tests and the rendered trust-plot preview verify the unavailable state.

entries.title: Mover/stayer trees counted the wrong group classes
entries.problem: Tree construction could rely on the nominal group-class field and omit the additional stayer posterior column.
entries.fix: Count the actual group posterior columns and carry the correct class labels into the tree.
entries.verification: A mover/stayer enumeration now produces the expected group-level tree; reporting regressions pass.

entries.title: Family enumeration lost requested search controls
entries.problem: Additive-family enumeration could fail to forward search and screening controls to its fits.
entries.fix: Forward the declared search method and screening budget consistently.
entries.verification: Regression checks verify requested controls reach the fitting path.

entries.title: ML three-step estimation missed a higher regular solution
entries.problem: The equal-variance step-three optimizer stopped at likelihood −7316.54473287439 while an independently verified regular point reached −7316.50817336643.
entries.fix: Add guarded BFGS candidates from existing starts in a bounded, standardized variance chart, with score, convergence and information checks. Retain the original tie policy.
entries.verification: The maximum public mean difference is 2.56 × 10⁻¹⁰ standard-error units; the maximum relative standard-error difference is 7.92 × 10⁻¹⁰. The full ML3 file passed 2,014 assertions and 6,328 comparison rows.

entries.title: Supporting scripts could fail or silently reshape incomplete results
entries.problem: A standalone runner used an unavailable helper before loading it; a recovery pivot could accept missing or duplicate parameter cells.
entries.fix: Resolve the CLI stage using base R before loading helpers, and require a complete, unique, finite parameter grid.
entries.verification: CLI and recovery regressions preserve structural zeros and reject absent or duplicated cells.

entries.title: Stability reporting could group results incorrectly
entries.problem: Rounded bins could separate equivalent likelihoods or merge values outside the intended tolerance; convergence was not a separate required result.
entries.fix: Group by bounded likelihood distance, validate seed inputs and report converged-fit counts explicitly.
entries.verification: Harness self-tests pass; the final eight-suite harness compares 1,021 quantities with all agreed.

entries.title: Comparison gates and summaries could overstate agreement
entries.problem: Nonfinite values, invalid tolerances or supplied agreement flags could yield misleading outcomes. Mixed quantities were presented as if all used printed rounding units.
entries.fix: Require valid finite comparisons, recompute agreement, and report each difference relative to its own tolerance and precision convention.
entries.verification: Negative-control self-tests pass; every final harness value, difference and tolerance is finite, and every tolerance is positive.

entries.title: External runners could accept stale or unsuccessful output
entries.problem: Shell entry/export behavior could fail when invoked through sh. Some collection paths could accept incomplete or stale program outputs.
entries.fix: Re-enter Bash where needed, preserve arguments safely, require normal Mplus termination and fresh fitted Latent GOLD listings/posteriors, and clear stale outputs.
entries.verification: Four Python fault/success tests use fake executables to verify the runner contracts; this does not claim fresh proprietary-engine fits.

entries.title: Research code bypassed fork safety checks
entries.problem: Direct mclapply calls in research scripts could run on unsafe Apple Accelerate or Windows configurations; a kit generator could otherwise delete retained inputs before failing.
entries.fix: Check the runtime before forking in 21 raw runners with 23 fork calls. The kit preflight runs before deletion, and the repaired search CLIs check before creating output directories. Fixed-seed ML3/VLMR helpers use tested serial dispatch on unsafe runtimes.
entries.verification: Scientific-code comparisons show unchanged budgets, seeds and worker calculations. Runtime/protocol tests pass; historical studies and kits were not regenerated.

entries.title: An inspection test assumed installed packages included source files
entries.problem: An installed package has an R directory without necessarily containing the original conditions.R source file.
entries.fix: Check for the actual source file before performing the source-inspection test.
entries.verification: The native installed-package check passes; source-only checks are explicitly skipped in that context and run in the source suite.

entries.title: Deferred features used retired services or weak data matching
entries.problem: The experimental random-intercept module depended on obsolete reporting/graphics helpers. The deferred LMR wrapper did not fully check data and objective compatibility.
entries.fix: Adapt reporting and plots to current services, register the deferred methods in-session, and strengthen data/weight/transformation checks.
entries.verification: All 78 deferred-module assertions pass. The deferred LMR prototype still deliberately has no p-value.

entries.title: The independent reference returned a worse last iterate
entries.problem: For huge_01, the reference EM accepted a tiny negative change as convergence and returned a likelihood 2.85 × 10⁻⁹ below its starting point.
entries.fix: Retain the complete best state, including the start; continue negative steps and converge only on a finite nonnegative gain below the unchanged tolerance. Record termination separately.
entries.verification: The exact case reaches zero gain at iteration 253. All 52 polish cases and the full four-file joint-item rerun pass.

entries.title: The poLCA comparator exhausted its iteration budget
entries.problem: All ten starts for twopair_mod_05 reached 20,000 iterations before meeting the requested tolerance, leaving five comparison rows outside tolerance.
entries.fix: Uniformly retain the original 20,000-cap run and add a 200,000-cap verification run for all 49 eligible cases, using the same seeds, starts and tolerance.
entries.verification: The difficult case converges at iteration 56,767. All 343 verification rows pass; the five original failures remain recorded. No verified case hits the larger cap.

entries.title: Default-search misses were confused with numerical equivalence
entries.problem: A direct-effects default search missed a higher regular likelihood by 8.499224. A joint-item fit met its per-step tolerance while still having about 1.2767 × 10⁻⁴ remaining likelihood gain.
entries.fix: Declare uniform comparison recipes: both kmeans and emEM for the direct-effects cases, and strict own-parameter resumes for joint items. Preserve the original fits and gaps separately.
entries.verification: All 5,727 direct-effects retained-reference rows pass. The joint-item verification covers 792 retained external rows, 343 poLCA rows and a 140-dataset independent study. The production defaults still have the documented limitations.

entries.title: Guides contained misleading descriptions and retired calls
entries.problem: Examples and prose misdescribed BCH weighting, thin-class heuristics, MAR implications, class matching and other conventions. An archived tutorial used retired API calls.
entries.fix: Correct the explanations and assumptions, update the tutorial to current calls and data semantics, and regenerate the affected help pages.
entries.verification: All 20 guides render, workflow-number tests pass, and the archived tutorial was rendered successfully during the repair verification.

entries.title: The supplied report overstated what was established
entries.problem: Its counts, additive/ordinal descriptions and VLMR sign convention contained errors; its universal compatibility, numerical and equivalence certifications lacked the necessary scope and execution evidence.
entries.fix: Write a claim-by-claim correction with source links, exact inventory counts and a dated verification ledger. Keep the original report unchanged.
entries.verification: The corrected review links the source and preserved evidence, distinguishing executed checks, source review, historical results and remaining limits.

entries.title: RNG restoration was promised too broadly
entries.problem: A NULL seed intentionally advances the caller stream; base R does not expose the cached Box–Muller normal value, so restoring .Random.seed cannot restore that hidden cache.
entries.fix: Qualify the exposed-state and explicit-seed contract in the documentation, without changing RNG kind to hide the limitation.
entries.verification: Seed-scope and reproducibility checks pass. Hidden-cache restoration remains a documented platform limitation.

entries.title: Shared covariance was described as universally safe from degeneracy
entries.problem: Sharing a covariance prevents an isolated component from collapsing independently, but atomic or over-extracted data can still drive the shared covariance to its floor.
entries.fix: Correct the search rationale and model documentation; retain boundary diagnostics and inference refusals.
entries.verification: A reproduced atomic-data example reaches the shared variance floor. The report now treats finite search, boundaries and global optimality as explicit limitations.
